Messages.Author: Disco_Stu
Messages.Body:
Hi all,

Okay, a different take on getting Sabbat vamps to bruise-vote their way to victory...

Imprimatur

Cost: 2
Requires an Archbishop, Cardinal, Priscus or Regent. Unique.
Only usable as an action is announced. If this action is successful, the acting vampire gains this card and untaps. This vampire has +1 strength and an additional vote. Burn this card at the end of your turn.

The Unique-ness means you wouldn't pack your deck with them (it effectively limits itself to one per turn), but they provide a Freak Drive-ish effect with a bonus for titled vamps.

cheers,

Disco Stu

Messages.Author: Ankha
Messages.Body:
I like it.

I would drop the "unique" aspect to simply state that only 1 can be played each turn.

Name: Imprimatur
Cardtype: Action modifier
Cost: 2 blood
Requires an archbishop, cardinal, priscus or regent. Only usable when the action is announced.
If this action is successful, the acting vampire untaps at the end of the action and gains +1 strength and an additional vote until the end of the turn. Only 1 Imprimatur can be played each turn.

Prince of Paris, France

TWO blood?

I mean.. ye I can see this being helpful in bruise/vote and everything, but I'm pretty sure it's not worth 2 blood. It doesn't even pay itself back with Voter Cap and +1 strength is not really going to suddenly make blockers back out where they would have tried/been able to block otherwise.

Only 1 per turn, I guess, is fine. It provides a (conditional) untap, so I guess a blood cost of 1 is fine. Two blood would make it wallpaper.

Messages.Author: Disco_Stu
Messages.Body:
Hi everyone,

Thanks for the feedback. I figured the Uniqueness was a nice short way of saying "may only play one per turn". It also (to some degree unintentionally) interacts with someone else who may be playing one on an Enkil Cog-ed minion, although that's highly unlikely to occur

My first attempt at this only cost 1 blood, but I added an extra blood to make it equivalent to Truth of a Thousand Lies. Dropping the "as action is declared" angle should balance it back up sufficiently.

cheers
Disco Stu
